description.plain:
Feetech STS3215-C001 is a 345:1 magnetic-encoder actuator for addressable robot-arm joints and feedback-based motion experiments. Its 12-bit magnetic encoder, metal gears and half-duplex serial interface bring position control and operating feedback into one compact servo.

The 345:1 reduction suits torque-oriented joint selection, while the TTL bus allows individual servo IDs and returned status data. It is a practical starting point for SO-ARM100/SO-ARM101 projects that specify this exact voltage and ratio.

For integrators building robot arms, grippers or multi-servo prototypes, the TTL serial bus provides a shared communication path with separately addressable actuators. Use the STS protocol and register map, set unique IDs, and size the motor supply for simultaneous movement rather than relying on a host USB port.

Features

  • Exact 345:1 configuration - The reduction ratio identifies the intended speed/load balance for this STS3215 suffix.
  • Voltage-specific performance - 19.5 kg·cm stall torque and 5 kg·cm rated torque at 7.4 V; these are different operating limits.
  • Magnetic position sensing - 12-bit feedback provides 4,096 positions per revolution, approximately 0.088° per step. This is encoder resolution, not guaranteed mechanical accuracy.
  • Addressable TTL communication - Digital packets use a half-duplex serial bus rather than conventional PWM pulse commands.
  • Configurable network settings - Servo IDs span 0-253; supported communication rates are 38,400 bps to 1 Mbps, with 1 Mbps listed as the factory default.
  • Operating feedback - Read position, speed, load, supply voltage, current and temperature through the supported STS commands.
  • Multiple motion modes - Position, speed and step-mode functions support joint control and experimental motion workflows when configured using the model documentation.
  • Compact mechanical package - A 45.2 × 24.7 × 35 mm body and 55 ± 1 g mass help with joint-envelope and moving-mass planning.
  • Metal gear transmission - Copper gears, ball bearings and a 25T output spline sit inside a PA+GF case.
  • Official development examples - Feetech provides SMS_STS examples for Arduino/ESP32; use the STS memory table when adapting a host application.

FAQ

How does this version differ from other STS3215 servos?

STS3215-C001 uses a 345:1 reduction with the performance values shown at 7.4 V. The comparison table separates the four configurations; do not select by housing appearance alone.

What supply voltage should I use?

The datasheet lists 4-7.4 V input and quotes the main performance figures at 7.4 V. Use a regulated supply and wiring appropriate for the motor current and the other devices on the bus.

Is the stall torque a continuous output rating?

No. The 19.5 kg·cm stall torque is a locked-rotor value. The separate rated torque is 5 kg·cm at 7.4 V; duty cycle, heat and linkage loads still need validation.

Does this servo accept a standard PWM control signal?

No. It uses digital packets on a half-duplex TTL serial bus. A PWM-only servo output or an RS485 transceiver is not a direct substitute for the required TTL interface.

Can several servos share one bus?

Yes, with distinct IDs, a common supported baud rate and correctly designed wiring. The power supply must support the combined dynamic current; the available ID range is not a guarantee of the physical bus capacity.

What feedback can the controller read?

The datasheet lists position, speed, load, input voltage, current and temperature feedback. Read these values using the matching STS register map and supported commands.

Does 0.088 degrees mean positioning accuracy?

No. Approximately 0.088° is the electronic resolution of the 12-bit encoder. Gear backlash, load, calibration and control settings also affect actual output positioning.

Which official programming examples should I use?

Use the SMS_STS examples in Feetech FTServo_Arduino for the STS family. SCSCL and HLSCL have different application layers and memory tables; do not copy their register definitions into an STS project.

What is included?

The STS3215-C001 Servo option contains one servo. The URT2 Test board option contains one FE-URT2-C001 test board, not a servo. These are separate options; a controller, arm structure and power supply are not included unless specified for the selected option.

What should I check before the first movement?

Check polarity, supply voltage, pinout, unique ID and baud rate. Start unloaded at low speed, check rotation direction and joint limits, and stop if the mechanism binds or the actuator heats excessively.
